text:
Asha (PM): Quick sync — putting together Q4 roadmap slice for long-term platform routing. Goal: decide prioritization for 'isolation corridors' (multi-tenant lanes + geo routing). Need clear launch criteria and top customer asks to commit to a pilot.
Diego (Eng): +1. can we keep it to 3 concrete deliverables? e.g., 1) policy DSL, 2) routing runtime hooks, 3) rollout playbook.
Maya (Arch): I'd add a compatibility matrix for model variants and quantization profiles. otherwise we end up with mismatches during canaries.
Liam (SRE): Operationally we need evacuation and soft-evict flow defined. SLOs for cross-region failover too. Without that oncall will block launch.
Sophie (Sales): From customers: two asks keep recurring: data residency + predictable latency. enterprise deals want contract language for region pinning and SLA on p95 token latency.
Jules (Customer Success): Also hearing requests for per-tenant burst caps and deterministic throttling — customers want to avoid noisy-neighbor spikes.
Asha (PM): Good notes. Proposal: prioritise surface-level policy DSL + routing runtime hooks in Q4 pilot, then full tenancy slicing + evacuation flows in Q1. Can we enumerate launch criteria now?
Diego (Eng): Draft launch criteria (quick):
```
- policy DSL v1: supports region, affinity, fallback
- runtime: ability to route by tenant tag + model family
- canary: safe fallback to compatible model variant
- infra: tenant-level KV cache invalidation
- tests: perf regression <5% p50, p95 < target
```
Maya (Arch): Add: telemetry hooks (per-route tracing, token-level cost) + migration plan for existing tenants.
Liam (SRE): Operational launch gates: playbook documenting evacuation steps, runbook for cross-region failover, automated chaos test passed once.
Sophie (Sales): Market gating: one pilot customer signed (legal ok with region pinning), documented SLA appendix, pricing for reserved lanes.
Jules (Customer Success): Also require migration checklist and a training session for customer ops + 2 internal runbooks.
Asha (PM): Nice. Now tradeoffs — cost vs isolation granularity. If we push hard for per-tenant dedicated lanes -> big infra delta. Option B: soft-isolation with strong rate-limits + QoS. Thoughts?
Diego (Eng): Option A increases bin packing complexity and cost. Option B is achievable faster and relies on runtime QoS and batching knobs. Might be okay for most customers.
Maya (Arch): For regulated customers we still need A (hard isolation) eventually. Suggest dual-path: ship B quickly as a general availability, keep A as enterprise premium.
Liam (SRE): Agree dual-path. But we must ensure routing fallback path when A fails back to B without data leakage. Documented in the playbook.
Sophie (Sales): That maps well to GTM: B = self-serve + dedicated pricing; A = enterprise contract + onboarding. Good.
Asha (PM): Dependencies — what blocks us? list from eng/infra/ops
Diego (Eng): kernel selection for affinity routing (infra), runtime metrics plumbing, policy DSL parser + stable protobufs.
Maya (Arch): Also need a small change to model registry to mark compatible fallback variants.
Liam (SRE): Networking changes for VPC pinning in Private mode, and KMS integration acceptance tests.
Asha (PM): Timeline ask: Can Eng produce a Q4 pilot alpha by end of quarter if we scope B-only? (no hard isolation)
Diego (Eng): If we scope B-only and reuse existing kernel paths, yes. Need 6 weeks for DSL + 4 weeks for runtime wiring + 2 weeks for canary infra = feasible.
Maya (Arch): I'll take ownership of compatibility matrix and model registry changes.
Liam (SRE): I'll draft evacuation playbook + chaos tests.
Sophie (Sales): I'll line up 2 pilot customers: one mid-market (interested in predictable latency) and one enterprise (wants roadmap for A).
Jules (Customer Success): I'll prep migration checklist and a customer-facing FAQ doc.
Asha (PM): Action items + owners:
- policy DSL v1 (Diego)
- runtime routing hooks (Diego + Maya)
- telemetry + compatibility matrix (Maya)
- evacuation runbook + chaos tests (Liam)
- pilot customer commitments (Sophie)
- migration & onboarding docs (Jules)
Due: Q4 EoQ alpha for B-path. If blockers appear, escalate to execs.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: infra/telemetry-proto bump -> scheduled 1747771260 :rocket: (automated)
Asha (PM): OK let's lock this. One more quick ask: what are the minimal SLA numbers to promise for pilot? suggestions?
Liam (SRE): Pilot SLA suggestion: p50 < 40ms (in-region), p95 < 220ms (in-region), cross-region p95 < 450ms. Also availability target 99.9% for dedicated lanes.
Sophie (Sales): Those look marketable. I'll check with finance for pricing math.
Diego (Eng): We'll instrument token-level latency and cost before pilot. Need to ensure billing accuracy for reserved lanes.
Maya (Arch): I'll add a short note on fallback semantics: when primary routing fails, fallback variants must preserve input privacy and use model variants with deterministic degradation.
Asha (PM): Great. I'll convert this thread into a short PRD and add the launch checklist. Thanks everyone — will sync weekly on progress. :spiral_calendar:
